paper: Jin, Zhang, Kevrekidis, Karniadakis — Learning Poisson systems and trajectories of autonomous systems via Poisson neural networks (arXiv:2012.03133, IEEE TNNLS 2022, DOI 10.1109/TNNLS.2022.3148734)
focal_experiment_replicated: Section IV-A Lotka–Volterra (REPLICATED, verdict from Argo argo:claude-opus-4.7)

open_questions.q: Does the composition Φ = INN ∘ SympNet ∘ INN⁻¹ genuinely preserve the underlying Poisson bracket to machine precision, or only approximately at the discrete-map level after training?
open_questions.basis: The Darboux–Lie construction guarantees Poisson preservation for the *exact* θ ∘ φ_H ∘ θ⁻¹ map, but the trained INN is only an approximate θ. Our rerun observed PNN invariant drift 5.81e-3 (max) and 1.41e-3 (at step 1000) on LV — clearly better than MLP (2.98e-2) but ~4 orders of magnitude looser than the SV symplectic integrator reference (4.77e-7). REPORT.md flags C1 as OUT-OF-SCOPE for rollout-based testing.
open_questions.next_steps: Directly measure the pullback bracket {f,g}_Φ − {f,g}_B for a battery of test functions (f,g) on a grid in phase space at successive training checkpoints; also compute the pushforward Jacobian J = ∂Φ/∂y and check the finite-dimensional condition J B(y) Jᵀ = B(Φ(y)) at random points, to separate architectural preservation from residual approximation error.

open_questions.q: How does PNN’s long-time stability degrade on truly non-separable Hamiltonians (e.g. H(p,q) = p²q² + V(q), Hénon–Heiles, or coupled anharmonic oscillators) where the G-SympNet symmetric-splitting motif is not obviously the right inductive bias?
open_questions.basis: The paper (and the LV replication here) uses a G-type SympNet on log-canonical coordinates, effectively a separable-friendly composition. REPORT.md restricts the tested experiment to LV; non-separable Hamiltonians are neither in the paper’s five demos nor in our C2/C3 tests.
open_questions.next_steps: Add a Hénon–Heiles rollout benchmark (well-known chaotic quartic Hamiltonian) with the same INN+G-SympNet stack, then swap in LA-SympNet and P-type variants; compare rollout MSE, invariant drift, and Poincaré-section reconstruction against a symplectic RK integrator ground truth.

open_questions.q: How does PNN compare head-to-head with Hamiltonian Neural Networks (HNN, Greydanus 2019) and bare SympNets on canonical Hamiltonian problems where all three architectures are applicable?
open_questions.basis: Our replication compared PNN only to an unstructured residual MLP (12,802 params, ~16× PNN). The paper motivates PNN as strictly *more general* than SympNet (which is Hamiltonian-only, and cannot even fit multi-trajectory LV in non-canonical form), but no controlled A/B against HNN or bare SympNet on a canonical Hamiltonian problem where all three are applicable is provided in REPORT.md, and this replication did not add one.
open_questions.next_steps: Design a two-degree-of-freedom canonical Hamiltonian benchmark (e.g. Kepler, double pendulum linearised regime), train PNN, bare LA-SympNet, HNN with an RK4 forward map, and the MLP baseline under matched parameter and training-iteration budgets; report rollout MSE, invariant drift, and orbit-closure error.

open_questions.q: How sensitive is the empirical replication verdict to the reduced training budget (30k vs the paper’s 200k iterations), and does an extended budget continue to reduce PNN drift or does it hit an INN-approximation floor?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md explicitly deviates by using 15% of the author iteration budget for wall-time reasons, and notes PNN step-1000 MSE (3.61e-3) is already smaller than step-100 MSE (4.89e-3) — the model is in a stable regime, but absolute error may or may not match the paper’s original level at 200k iterations. C2/C3 are qualitatively unchanged, but no plateau-vs-budget curve is measured.
open_questions.next_steps: Rerun PNN at {30k, 100k, 200k, 500k} iterations with 5 seeds each; plot rollout-MSE and max-invariant-drift vs iteration; fit a power-law / plateau and report whether an approximation floor exists below which more training does not help.

open_questions.q: Does PNN generalise off the trained level curves — i.e. can it accurately roll out initial conditions on nearby but unseen orbits of the same LV system, or is stability contingent on starting *on* the training endpoints?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md §GENUINE CRITIQUE notes rollouts start from the three training endpoints, which lie ON the trained level curves. All reported rollout-MSE and invariant-drift numbers are therefore in-basin. The Poisson-structure story implies structural generalisation across the whole phase space, but this was not tested in this replication.
open_questions.next_steps: Sample initial conditions on a grid of level curves H = c for c not in the training set (e.g. c between the trained closed orbits, and c well outside them); measure 1000-step rollout MSE and invariant drift per level curve; compare against the MLP baseline on the same grid to isolate structural vs interpolative generalisation.
